data.narrative:
Forge Nano is a Series C climate and energy company that has raised $40M to date. The valuation analysis employs two methods triangulated against a peer set of three same-sector, same-stage private companies (KoBold Metals at $3.0B, Electric Hydrogen at $1.0B, and Amogy at $700M), supplemented by a broader comp universe of nine private peers and one public comparable.

The Stage-Progression method applies a 1.7x step-up multiplier typical of Series C advancement to the $40M total raised proxy, implying a $68M valuation. The Peer-Median method uses the three direct comparables and yields a $1.0B implied valuation, with the peer range spanning $700M to $3.0B. These two methods produce materially divergent signals, reflecting the wide dispersion in recent Climate & Energy valuations at this stage.

Triangulating both approaches yields a range of $58M (low) to $1.1B (high), with a median of $534M. The stage-progression floor reflects capitalized deployment; the peer-derived ceiling reflects higher risk appetite in the climate capital stack. Key uncertainties include technology readiness, path to revenue, and whether Forge Nano's intellectual property and market position align with the upper-quartile peers (KoBold, Electric Hydrogen) or lower-quartile (Amogy). Substantial valuation sensitivity exists to commercialization trajectory and competitive differentiation within the energy transition sector.
